results.controlIntent: a. Identify flaws in the system; report those system flaws; and correct those system flaws; b. Before installation, test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness; and test those updates for potential side effects; c. Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of the release of the updates; and d. Incorporate flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals two distinct flaw-remediation control failures:

**1. Hotfix deployed outside the change-control/registry process (SI-2.r1.d)**
The UpdateEndpoint event (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z, `8ecfe9ca`) applied a hotfix configuration (`churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`) to the live endpoint with *no corresponding model registry entry*. The model registry (`c0679254`) contains only version 1, approved on 2025-12-01. This means the hotfix — which is precisely the kind of flaw-remediation update SI-2 governs — was never registered, reviewed, or formally approved. This is a direct violation of SI-2.r1(d), which requires flaw remediation to be incorporated into the organizational configuration management process.

**2. Ambiguous ordering of initial deployment vs. approval (SI-2.r1.b/c)**
The CreateEndpoint event (`ae9c0d27`) is timestamped 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z, while registry approval occurred at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z. The event note flags this as a pre-approval deployment, but the raw timestamps show the endpoint was created *after* approval. This inconsistency could indicate a data integrity issue in the audit trail, or that the note is erroneous — either way it warrants human review.

**Primary finding:** The unregistered hotfix deployment is a clear, high-confidence violation of SI-2.r1(d). Flaw remediation (the hotfix) was applied to a production endpoint without going through the model registry or any documented approval workflow, circumventing the configuration management process entirely.
gaps: No registry entry exists for the hotfix model package — it is impossible to verify whether the hotfix was tested for effectiveness or side effects (SI-2.r1.b) before deployment.
No patch/vulnerability tracking system data is available to confirm whether flaws were formally identified and reported (SI-2.r1.a).
No SLA or policy document is available to assess whether the hotfix was applied within the organization-defined time period (SI-2.r1.c).
Human attestation is needed to resolve the conflicting timestamp/note discrepancy in the CreateEndpoint event.
No evidence of pre-deployment testing records for either the initial model or the hotfix.
